title: Batch retrieve documents
description: Retrieve up to 100 permission-visible indexed documents in one experimental Platform Documents batch, mixing document IDs and URLs, and read partial misses from warnings.

codeWalkthrough.intro: The example signs in with @gleanwork/auth and calls the experimental Documents HTTP API. The published TypeScript API client does not include these operations. client.documents is a different API.

examples.title: Post a mixed batch
examples.description: Resolve the backend, take a documents:read token from the auth package, and send X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true on the request. POST /api/documents/batch with 1 to 100 document_specs. Each spec is exactly one of document_id or url. include CONTENT is a body field, not a query parameter.

examples.title: Read results and warnings
examples.description: Found selectors are results. Complete misses are warnings on the same HTTP 200, each with code, message, and context.index. Every spec index appears in exactly one of those arrays. A warning does not fail the command. An HTTP error fails the whole batch.

prerequisites: A Glean instance with indexed documents you can open
Your work email, or the complete Glean backend HTTPS origin
The documents:read OAuth scope, or a user-scoped token with permission to read documents
One document URL and one document ID for documents you can open

demoQueries.query: Retrieve a document URL and a document ID you can open, plus one URL that is not indexed
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Prints Retrieved N of M documents, the request_id, a results list, and a warnings list. A selector the server cannot resolve is a warning on HTTP 200, and the command exits 0. HTTP errors, including 400 and 413, exit non-zero and do not print the Retrieved line. With --content, each result also includes the content segment count. An empty full_text_list is success and means there is no extracted text.

codeAssets.description: TypeScript CLI that retrieves indexed documents by a mix of IDs and URLs in one batch

steps.title: Copy the project onto your machine
steps.description: Copy the runnable TypeScript CLI and its fixture tests into a new directory. Sign-in uses the official `@gleanwork/auth` package.

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.description: Enter the project directory and install its dependencies. Run the remaining commands from this directory.

steps.title: Run the fixture tests
steps.description: Run the tests without credentials or network access. They call the HTTP client through MSW and fail on unhandled requests. Passing tests does not prove access to your Glean instance.

steps.title: Choose an authentication path
steps.description: OAuth is the default. `@gleanwork/auth` discovers your instance, registers the OAuth client dynamically, and stores credentials outside the project. If OAuth is unavailable, copy `.env.example` to `.env`, set `GLEAN_SERVER_URL` and a user-scoped `GLEAN_API_TOKEN` with permission to read documents, and skip the next step. Omit `--email` from the remaining commands. If email discovery finds the wrong instance, replace `--email` with `--server-url` and your complete backend HTTPS origin.

steps.title: Sign in with OAuth
steps.description: Run the login command with the `documents:read` scope and finish authorization in your browser. Wait until the command reports success. Skip this step when you configured a token in `.env`.

steps.title: Verify against your instance
steps.description: Send one URL and one document ID for documents you can open. The command prints `Retrieved N of M documents`, the `request_id`, and the `results` and `warnings` lists. With a token in `.env`, omit `--email`.

steps.title: Include a miss and extracted text
steps.description: Repeat the two selectors, add a URL that is not an indexed document, and pass `--content`. The client sends `include` as `CONTENT` in the JSON body. A complete miss is a warning on HTTP 200, and the command still exits 0. The warning code and message come from the server. With a token, omit `--email`.

questions.prompt: What is your work email address?
What is the URL of a document you can open in Glean?
What is the document ID of a document you can open in Glean?

aiPrompt: Scaffold and run the experimental Documents batch quickstart. Ask for the work email, one document URL the caller can open in Glean, and one document_id. Run the fixture tests before authentication. Sign in with the official glean-auth CLI from @gleanwork/auth using the documents:read scope, or set GLEAN_SERVER_URL and a user-scoped GLEAN_API_TOKEN with documents:read. Do not add a scope-fallback wrapper and do not request any other scope. The published @gleanwork/api-client package has no Platform Documents operations. Do not call client.documents; that is a different API. Call the HTTP API with fetch. Send X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true on every request. These operations are experimental, and the server hides them without that header. POST /api/documents/batch with document_specs of 1 to 100 items. Each item is exactly one of document_id or url. Found documents are results. Complete misses are warnings on HTTP 200, with code, message, and context.index. Example codes are resource_not_found and invalid_parameter. A 200 with warnings exits 0, including when every selector misses. HTTP errors fail the command. HTTP 400 rejects a bad request shape. HTTP 413 means the body is too large. More than 100 selectors is rejected before the request. include CONTENT goes in the JSON body only with --content. It adds content.full_text_list on every found document. An empty list means no extracted text. A content failure fails the whole batch. Gmail and Outlook caller-specific citation IDs are not document_id selectors; send a URL instead. That URL can still be a resource_not_found warning. Federated results and go-link shortcuts are not retrievable. Do not teach per-item status enums. Print request_id. Never log tokens.
llmContext: Use @gleanwork/auth 1.0.0 and the documents:read scope. @gleanwork/api-client has no Platform Documents operations, and client.documents is a different API. POST /api/documents/batch with fetch and send X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true. Send 1 to 100 document_specs, each exactly one of document_id or url. results are hits. warnings are misses on HTTP 200 and the command still exits 0. HTTP errors fail it. include CONTENT is optional. Gmail and Outlook IDs need a URL. Federated results and go links are not retrievable. Do not log tokens or teach per-item status enums.

content.problem: You already have a mix of document IDs and URLs, and you need the indexed records the caller can see without one round trip per document. One experimental Platform Documents batch accepts 1 to 100 selectors and returns found documents in results and complete misses in warnings. The published TypeScript API client does not include these operations, so this example calls the HTTP API and uses the official auth package for sign-in.
takeItFurther: Pass --content when you need extracted text. include CONTENT in the JSON body adds content.full_text_list on every found document. An empty list means Glean stored no extracted text. A failure to read requested content fails the whole batch.
Use the retrieve-by-URL recipe when you have one URL and want to confirm the returned document_id reads back the same document.
Keep indexed store IDs. Do not send a Gmail or Outlook caller-specific citation ID as document_id. Send that document's URL instead.

guardrails.title: Send the experimental header on every request
guardrails.rule: Set X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true. Without it, the server hides these operations. This client sets the header in one place so a new call cannot skip it.

guardrails.title: Request only documents:read
guardrails.rule: OAuth login and the token provider use the documents:read scope. Do not add other scopes. A user-scoped token is the fallback when OAuth is unavailable, and it needs permission to read documents.

guardrails.title: Treat warnings as a successful batch
guardrails.rule: HTTP 200 with warnings means the batch completed and some selectors missed. Exit 0 and print both results and warnings. Exit non-zero only when the request itself fails, including HTTP 400, 401, 403, 404, 413, and 429.

limitations.title: Experimental API
limitations.description: These operations are experimental and can change. Callers that omit X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true do not see them. The published @gleanwork/api-client package has no Platform Documents methods. client.documents reads documents through a different API; do not substitute it here.

limitations.title: Some documents are not retrievable
limitations.description: Gmail and Outlook search results and chat citations can carry caller-specific IDs. The batch does not accept those IDs as document_id. Send a URL selector instead. That URL can still come back as a resource_not_found warning. Federated results and go-link shortcuts are not retrievable. You only receive documents visible to the caller.

limitations.title: A miss is a warning, not a per-item status
limitations.description: Each selector lands in results or warnings. Warning code and message are strings from the server. resource_not_found and invalid_parameter are examples, not a closed list, and there is no per-item status field. An empty or malformed URL is a warning after a complete read, not an HTTP 400. The CLI rejects a blank flag before it sends the request. HTTP 413 means the body is too large. Sending more than 100 selectors is rejected locally and is not the 413 case.

limitations.title: Content is extracted text, not the file
limitations.description: include CONTENT adds content.full_text_list on every found document. The list is empty when Glean has no extracted text after a complete read. If requested content cannot be read, the batch fails instead of returning documents without content. The CLI prints the segment count, not every segment.
